title: Prescription Insurance on File Schedule of Approved-Claim History Credit on a Renewal Appeal
content:
Under **Prescription Insurance on File**, an appeal against a prior authorization denial earns a continuity credit that takes days off the appeal decision window, according to how many claims have been paid on the coverage for the appealed drug under a prior authorization approval. The appealed drug is the prescription the most recent denial on the coverage concerns.

## Schedule

| Claims paid on the coverage for the appealed drug under a prior authorization approval | Days taken off the appeal decision window |
|---|---|
| 12 or more | 5 |
| At least 6 but fewer than 12 | 2 |
| Fewer than 6 | 0 |

## Notes to the schedule

1. The count is of claims paid on the coverage for the appealed drug on the approved-prior-authorization basis, as the claim history shows them. Claims for other prescriptions, and claims for the appealed drug paid on any other basis, are not counted.
2. The bands meet at 6 and 12 claims: 5 claims takes nothing off; 6 claims takes 2 days off; 11 claims takes 2 days off; 12 claims takes 5 days off.

## Illustrations (hypothetical claim histories)

- Fourteen approved claims for the appealed drug on the coverage, plus three routine claims for another drug: 14 counted, 5 days off.
- Eight approved claims for the appealed drug: 2 days off.
- Four approved claims for the appealed drug and two transition fills for it: 4 counted, nothing off.
